_why_two_claims: AGREEMENT asks whether the engines compute the same thing; RECOVERY asks whether they compute the right thing. Neither implies the other.

truth.source: the fixture's data-generating process: risks 0.5 and 0.2, odds ratio 4

agreement.claim: both engines report the same conditional odds ratio, exact interval (log scale), sample odds ratio and p-value
agreement._note: The conditional MLE and its exact bounds are roots of monotone equations, and R (uniroot at its default tolerance) and scipy stop at slightly different points. Measured on the log scale: the estimate agrees to 1.6e-6; the bounds differed by 3.2e-5 and 2.1e-4 on a 60-per-group fixture and by 9.7e-6 and 1.07e-4 on this one. The bounds' tolerance is 1e-3, about five times the largest observed. On the odds-ratio scale the upper bound's gap is larger (1.8e-3 at 27.1 on a 30-per-group fixture), which is why the bounds are emitted on the log scale. The p-value and the sample odds ratio agree exactly. harness/categorical_examples.test.py checks the estimate against the Fisher noncentral hypergeometric mean equation.

recovery.claim: the conditional log odds ratio is close to the one the fixture was built with

calibration.limits: Measured by harness/categorical_examples.test.py over seeds 0 to 99. At 30 and 60 per group the 99th percentile misses (1.34, 1.09) reached log(4) itself, so a null effect would have passed; the fixture was enlarged to 120 per group for that reason.
